feedback.problem: A data set contains the observations ${x}_{1}=28,{x}_{2}=37$ with $z$-scores ${z}_{1}=0.8$ and ${z}_{2}=1.2,$ respectively. Find the standard deviation of the data set.
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+0.8\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}37 & =\overset{¯}{x}+1.2\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the first equation from the second and solving for $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(37-28) & =(1.2-0.8)\cdot \sigma  \\ 9 & =0.4\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =22.5.\end{aligned}
$$
